evidence_tier: ★ COACHING. This artifact is a READING, not a measurement. Every figure is sourced (◆ deck-facts / deck-audit / goldfish_metrics.json / mana_analysis.json / benchmark.json / bracket_report.json, or a checker-passed stack); every framework claim carries the strategy:<id> it came from and its quote is verbatim from the section fetched with lookup-strategy this session. A strategy citation never upgrades a line to rules-verified, and not one candidate line below is a fact.
mandate: Written against v1.3.0 (decklist_sha256 99419d5b9145), the seven-swap protection package from prescription 0241fb6a70f1, plus the 2026-09-17 paper rescan that corrected five cards. The frame it replaces was stamped 5611a822851c — THREE versions behind — and its headline claim, that an oracle scan for 'counter target' returned nothing, is now FALSE. The pilot's brief is unchanged (pilot_feedback.md, 2026-07-28: bracket 4 approved, 'mean, consistent, validated, powerfully scary'), and the computed floor is still 3 'Upgraded' on two Game Changers (bracket_report.json: Enlightened Tutor, Teferi's Protection; target 4, within_target true — Worldly Tutor was the third and V6 cut it). What this frame is written against is the pilot's own verdict after six logged games at 2W 4L: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close', and 'I now have zero responses'. The first half is still true. The second half is no longer true, and the frame's job is to say what the first half now costs.
archetype: Five-colour Dragon typal ramp-into-entry-triggers with an instant-speed answer package bolted on at v1.3.0 — a linear deck buying back some of the flexibility strategy:critical-mass says it sold. ◆ deck-facts at 99419d5b9145: 97 entries / 100 copies, 35 land copies over 32 land entries, 65 nonland entries, 32 creature entries of which 24 carry Dragon in the type line (the commander and Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar included). Acceleration is 23 ramp copies (deck-audit, verdict 'over' against 10-12), of which 5 are cost reducers stacking under eminence. The answer half is now countable: deck-audit reads interaction 11 copies inside a 22-copy interactive suite, verdict 'at' — and benchmark.json reads answer_cards 22, answer_share 0.2292, classes_covered 7 of 15. Written without an archetype keyword on purpose: deck_audit._ARCHETYPE_HINTS keyword-matches this string and the base ratio targets are the right yardstick for a list with 32 creature entries.

the_claim_tested.claim: V6's thesis, in the pilot's framing: shift from DEPLOY ON YOUR TURN AND TELEGRAPH to DEPLOY AT THE END OF THE TURN BEFORE YOURS. Four of the six additions work at instant speed — Stubborn Denial is an instant; Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar each print Flash (oracle text, cards.json). Asceticism {3}{G}{G} and Steel Hellkite {6} do not.
the_claim_tested.verdict: THE LITERATURE SUPPORTS IT, ON THREE INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, AND NAMES TWO CONDITIONS UNDER WHICH IT BACKFIRES. It is not a tempo claim in the doc's vocabulary — it is a threat-assessment claim, which is what the pilot suspected.
supported_because: THE ANSWER TO ARCHENEMY IS THE OPEN MANA ITSELF, NOT THE CARD YOU CAST WITH IT. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management ends on exactly this sentence: "Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction." That is a 3-to-1 return on a resource the 1-to-3 disadvantage otherwise taxes (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry: "you spend a card, one opponent loses a card, and two bystanders profit from the exchange for free"). Held mana is the only thing this deck owns that is asymmetric in its favour.

END-OF-TURN-BEFORE-YOURS IS THE DOC'S NAMED DEFAULT, NOT AN INVENTION. strategy:tempo.sequencing's Commander correction: "you are sequencing around three responders — count each seat's open mana separately, and prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent." Flash converts that from a preference into a legal option for 28 of the deck's other 96 entries (see flash_grant_scope). It also satisfies strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's operative rule — "Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress" — because a Dragon that arrives in the last end step before your untap cannot be assessed for a full rotation, only for your own turn.

IT BUYS BACK THE DEFLECTION BUDGET THE ENGINE SPENDS. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: "The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out." Games 003 and 004 are that budget running out early — log.jsonl 003, 'once the table read "Sean is swinging for 28 in the air" they converged immediately'; 004, 'the treasure pile plus fireballing every ETB made me the obvious problem. David called it out, the table converged'. Deploying at instant speed does not make the board smaller; it makes the board VISIBLE for fewer opponent decision points, which is what the budget is denominated in. And strategy:information.range-tells makes held mana do offensive work for free: "Held lands plus instant-speed pace means interaction until proven otherwise" and "Representing is the offensive half: keep open the mana for the trick you don't have."
backfires_when: YOU HOLD AND DO NOT ACT — 'PLAYING SCARED'. strategy:resource-hedging is blunt: "playing *scared* is paying real equity to dodge specific cards — handing a control deck free draw steps by refusing to commit — and it loses games the opponent never had the card in." This deck's pilot has already filed the failure mode in both directions. log.jsonl 005: 'I do not like having unspent mana, so I pour it into the board too early and telegraph' — the commit-too-early error V6 targets. log.jsonl 006: 'When Stephen targeted the dragon I had Return of the Wildspeaker in hand... I did not tap Tender, did not cast it, and let the removal resolve... I was too passive and did not pause to respond' — the hold-and-freeze error V6 CREATES MORE OPPORTUNITIES FOR. Note the card in that story is one of the seven V6 cut, so the specific line is gone; the habit is not. strategy:tempo states the diagnostic: "if you regularly end turns with unspent mana and no plan for it, your curve or your sequencing is wrong." The plan must be named before the mana is held.

YOU ARE THE LINEAR DECK AND THE HELD MANA DELAYS THE THRESHOLD. strategy:critical-mass: "linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power" and "interaction slots are the price of the engine, so the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers." strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance prices the same trade honestly: "protection slots and held mana cost you every game, removal only costs you some — against light-interaction pods, skip the insurance, pay the tax, rebuild." ◆ goldfish at 99419d5b9145 (10,000 iterations, seed 42) says the tax is affordable but not free: mean available mana 4.911 / 5.948 / 6.746 on turns four to six, against a Transcendent Dragon that costs {3}{U}{U} under eminence and a Whirlwing that costs {3}{U}. Holding for those two IS the turn on turns four and five.

THE ANSWER ROTS, OR IS SPENT ON SOMEONE ELSE'S PROBLEM. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: "The countervailing risk: held answers rot — against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now", and Rice's rule, "hold single-target removal until the threat is pointed at you — every one-for-one you cast in multiplayer is a net gift to the bystanders." Stubborn Denial and Swords to Plowshares are one-for-ones; countering a spell aimed at a third seat is the textbook gift.

THE BLUFF STOPS BEING RESPECTED. strategy:information.range-tells: "Weight inaction heaviest — what they did NOT do with mana available is the strongest signal", and the Commander correction, "your image persists — a pod remembers which bluffs you run and which fears you exploit, so tells and credibility are multi-game resources to manage deliberately." This is a five-player group that plays together weekly (log.jsonl 002, 003, 005 all at Oliver's with the same names). Representing interaction you never have is a multi-game resource being spent down, and strategy:multiplayer.politics' craft rule applies to it: "never lie outright about game state (credibility is a multi-game resource)."
the_claim_tested.the_condition_that_decides_it: Both the support and the backfire reduce to one question the doc asks twice: is the held mana attached to a NAMED plan for this rotation? strategy:tempo.sequencing — "think through the entire turn before doing anything"; strategy:pivot-point — "hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after." The operational test for this list, from strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's bar ("protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for"): before passing with mana up, say out loud which card it is for and which seat's action triggers it. If the answer is 'in case', that is strategy:resource-hedging's scared line and the mana should have been a Dragon.

flash_grant_scope.claim: Whirlwing Stormbrood's grant — 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash' (oracle text, front face) — covers 28 of the deck's 96 other entries, ENUMERATED, not estimated: 23 other Dragon-type entries (of 24 total, itself excluded) and 5 other sorceries (Crux of Fate, Desolation of Smaug, Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim).
flash_grant_scope.does_not_cover: 7 enchantment entries (Asceticism, Breaching Dragonstorm, Dragon Tempest, Garruk's Uprising, Roiling Dragonstorm, Sneak Attack, Temur Ascendancy) and 11 artifact entries (Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Dragon's Hoard, Herald's Horn, Lightning Greaves, Mithril Coat, Panharmonicon, Sol Ring, Steel Hellkite, Talisman of Dominance, Urza's Incubator). Mithril Coat and Steel Hellkite are on that list and are unaffected — the Coat prints its own Flash, the Hellkite does not. Two of the three tells the pilot named in log.jsonl 003 and 004 (Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge; Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm; Terror of the Peaks) are Dragons and ARE covered; Panharmonicon and Temur Ascendancy, which make those tells convert, are not.
flash_grant_scope.unevidenced: FORGE CANNOT LOAD WHIRLWING STORMBROOD — 'an unsupported card was requested', logged 14 times per the pilot's notes. I confirmed the negative side of that independently: the string 'Whirlwing' does not appear anywhere in the seven Forge logs under data/decks/ur-dragon/experiments/logs/working-vs-@final-v2-...-n167/. So the mechanism the whole V6 posture rests on has never been simulated and cannot be by this harness. Treat every claim about the flash grant — including the three grounded paragraphs above — as ★ coaching over oracle text, never ◆ measured.
flash_grant_scope.consequence_for_the_frame: Whirlwing costs {3}{U} under eminence and is a 4/4 flier that must RESOLVE and SURVIVE for the grant to matter. The posture is therefore available in two tiers: TIER 1 (always available, no card required) is the four printed instant-speed cards plus the nine other instants; TIER 2 (Whirlwing resolved) extends it to 28 more entries. Plan the game on tier 1 and treat tier 2 as upside — strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's warning applies, "the ceiling build runs one spectacular finisher and loses when it's answered."

role_assignment.default_role: STILL THE FAST SEAT, AND V6 DID NOT CHANGE THAT — IT CHANGED WHAT THE FAST SEAT CAN DO ON THE TURNS IT IS NOT ATTACKING. strategy:whos-the-beatdown: "the roles are set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label", and the game state this list creates is fast. ◆ goldfish at 99419d5b9145 (10,000 iterations, seed 42): mean available mana 3.614 / 4.911 / 5.948 / 6.746 on turns three to six, mean board power 9.755 at turn five and 14.877 at turn six, kill_by_turn_6 0.297, median kill turn 7, kill_by_turn_8 0.825. Apply strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's own table test — "picture turn 15 with both players on their best draws — whoever likes that picture less should be attacking now" — and the answer is unchanged, because the refuel did not move: deck-audit still reads card-advantage 4 copies against the ratio floor of 10, verdict 'under'. You are the beatdown from roughly turn four. WHAT IS NEW is that strategy:whos-the-beatdown's Commander correction is now ACTIONABLE rather than aspirational: "role is seat-relative — you can be the beatdown against one opponent and the control against another in the same turn cycle; assign per-threat, not per-game." With 14 instant-speed entries (11 instants: Boros Charm, Chaos Warp, Deflecting Swat, Enlightened Tutor, Flawless Maneuver, Generous Gift, Heroic Intervention, Sarkhan's Triumph, Stubborn Denial, Swords to Plowshares, Teferi's Protection; plus 3 with Flash: Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar) the deck can finally hold the control role against one seat while racing another. At v1.0.2 it could not. CAVEAT: the goldfish has no blockers, no removal and no opponents, so every speed figure above is a resource-development ceiling, not a table forecast.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: TWO LEGS, UNCHANGED IN SHAPE, WITH LEG 2 NOW PARTLY BUYABLE. (1) BOARD — a per-Dragon damage payoff (Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas) plus a widener (Miirym Sentinel Wyrm, Lathliss Dragon Queen, Ancient Gold Dragon) plus a haste source if the plan needs combat (Temur Ascendancy, Dragon Tempest on a flier, Lightning Greaves, Sneak Attack). ◆ goldfish prices leg 1 at 0.179 assembled / 0.109 by turn six (entry kill) and 0.274 / 0.186 (combat kill) — both labelled UNVERIFIED in goldfish_targets.json because no passing stack covers either. (2) TABLE — strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's bar, verbatim: the window opens when the attempt "can't be profitably answered — protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for", and "assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing." Leg 2 failed on 2026-09-01 and again on 2026-09-03. V6 buys the 'protection up' clause: ◆ goldfish's own target, 'Protection or a RESPONSE held for the big turn (v1.3.0 added three: Asceticism, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial)', reads 0.811 assembled / 0.713 by turn six, mean turn 2.58. It buys nothing about 'table tapped out' or 'interaction counted', which stay the pilot's job. strategy:pivot-point: "hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after."

engines.piece: Eminence + Urza's Incubator, Dragonspeaker Shaman, Herald's Horn, Dragonlord's Servant
engines.engine: IGNITION. Five cost reducers stacking with the commander's eminence, which is live from the command zone on turn one with nothing to remove. Every Dragon shifts left by one before any of the printed reducers land. This is why Transcendent Dragon reads {3}{U}{U} and Whirlwing {3}{U} in this deck rather than {4}{U}{U} and {4}{U}.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json) + ◆ goldfish at 99419d5b9145: 'Cost reducer drawn' 0.521 assembled / 0.421 by turn six, mean turn 3.26 (0.670 / 0.558 with tutors counted)

engines.engine: THE ARRIVAL, NOT THE ATTACK — the rebuilt engine model's thesis, and the doc agrees with it. 'Whenever one or more Dragons you control attack, draw that many cards, then you may put a permanent card from your hand onto the battlefield' (oracle text). The draw is the refuel on an axis deck-audit calls 'under' at 4 copies against 10; the put-into-play is a free deployment that dodges every counterspell at the table. strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's standard — "Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game" — is met by the trigger and by almost nothing else in the list.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json) + ◆ goldfish: commander cast by turn six 0.333, median cast turn 7 — the engine is a minority-of-games event and the deck must be able to win without it

engines.engine: THE ONE-MANA TAX THAT MAKES HOLDING MANA CHEAP. 'Counter target noncreature spell unless its controller pays {1}. Ferocious — If you control a creature with power 4 or greater, counter that spell instead' (oracle text). FEROCIOUS IS LIVE OFF 21 OF THE 32 CREATURE ENTRIES, ENUMERATED FROM cards.json: The Ur-Dragon 10, Ancient Gold Dragon 7, Drakuseth 7, Old Gnawbone 7, Atarka 6, Hellkite Courser 6, Lathliss 6, Miirym 6, Gadrak 5, Scourge of the Throne 5, Solphim 5, Steel Hellkite 5, Terror of the Peaks 5, Atsushi 4, Glorybringer 4, Goldspan Dragon 4, Scourge of Valkas 4, Smaug the Magnificent 4, Thunderbreak Regent 4, Transcendent Dragon 4, Whirlwing Stormbrood 4. The 11 that do not turn it on are the mana half (Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Delighted Halfling, Dragonlord's Servant, Dragonspeaker Shaman, Faeburrow Elder, Ignoble Hierarch) plus Firespitter Whelp, Ganax, Thrakkus the Butcher and Twinflame Tyrant. THE HANDBOOK IS WRONG ON THE DENOMINATOR: poh_procedures says '21 of 30'; the numerator is right and the denominator is 32. One further precision the count hides — one of the 21 is the commander, who is on the battlefield to turn ferocious on in 0.333 of goldfish runs by turn six, so the in-the-99 figure is 20 of 31.
engines.evidence: oracle text + cards.json power enumeration (all 32 creature entries read); ◆ deck-facts counts 32 creature entries; ◆ goldfish commander cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.333

engines.engine: CONSTANT PROTECTION AT FLASH SPEED — the tier strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance says an engine hub justifies: "constant protection (boots-style equipment and enchantments — always on, cheap to re-arm, useless against wraths)". 'Flash. Indestructible. When Mithril Coat enters, attach it to target legendary creature you control. Equipped creature has indestructible. Equip {3}' (oracle text). It costs {3} generic, so it is castable off any mana this five-colour deck has — which matters when mana_analysis reads black on-curve at 0.729 with rocks and dorks and 0.524 on lands alone. At v1.0.2 this tier contained Lightning Greaves alone, whose shroud also blocks your own targeting.
engines.evidence: oracle text; ◆ mana_analysis.json on_curve_probability; ◆ deck-audit protection axis 10 copies, verdict 'over'. THE PILOT'S FORGE FIGURE (cast 40 / activated 35 in a 177-game standard-v3 run) COULD NOT BE VERIFIED FROM A COMMITTED ARTIFACT — see gaps.

engines.engine: THE SCALPEL SWEEPER, and the one addition that is NOT instant speed and does not pretend to be. '{X}: Destroy each nonland permanent with mana value X whose controller was dealt combat damage by this creature this turn' (oracle text). deck-audit now counts it as this deck's second sweeper (with Crux of Fate), verdict 'at' against strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's "wipes 'one or two max' (Zupke caps at 3)". It is also the deck's answer to strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's breadth instruction — "cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any" — because X is chosen on resolution and hits artifacts and enchantments the rest of the suite reaches twice each (deck-audit interaction-breadth by_class: artifact 2, creature 6, enchantment 2, graveyard 0, land 1).
engines.evidence: oracle text; ◆ deck-audit sweepers axis (Crux of Fate, Steel Hellkite) verdict 'at', interaction-breadth 4 of 5 classes verdict 'under'. THE PILOT'S FORGE FIGURE (cast 36 / activated 53) COULD NOT BE VERIFIED FROM A COMMITTED ARTIFACT — see gaps.

engines.engine: A COUNTERSPELL THAT IS ALSO A BODY — exactly the "flexible modal slots that are never dead" tier of Cullen's taxonomy in strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance. 'Flash. Flying. When this creature enters, if you cast it, counter target spell...' (oracle text). Two scope limits the frame must carry: the counter is an ETB TRIGGER, so it can be responded to and it does nothing if the Dragon is countered or removed in response; and the 'if you cast it' clause means Sneak Attack and the commander's put-into-play do NOT get the counter. It costs {3}{U}{U} under eminence against 5.948 mean mana at turn five.
engines.evidence: oracle text; ◆ goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn t5 5.948, t6 6.746; ◆ goldfish interaction_castable_by_turn 0.311 / 0.415 / 0.510 on turns four to six (a FLOOR by the model's own note)

engines.engine: THE STATIC HALF OF THE PACKAGE, and the one that does the deflection work silently. 'Creatures you control have hexproof. {1}{G}: Regenerate target creature' (oracle text). Hexproof over a board of entry-trigger Dragons is the answer to the convergence in log.jsonl 003 and 004 — three seats' worth of single-target removal becomes uncastable at once, which is the asymmetric effect strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry asks for. It is sorcery speed at {3}{G}{G}, so it is a DEPLOY-EARLY card in a package otherwise built to deploy late, and it is the one V6 addition that reads as defensive on the board — strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: "deploy engines that read as defensive".
engines.evidence: oracle text; ◆ mana_analysis on_curve_probability G 0.907 with rocks and dorks, 0.831 lands only — the deck's best colour, so the double-green is affordable

engines.engine: FREE RESPONSES WITH A PRECONDITION THE DECK MEETS IN A MINORITY OF GAMES. Both read 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost' (oracle text). ◆ goldfish: commander cast by turn six 0.333, median cast turn 7. So on the turns V6's posture is about — four through six — these are {2}{R} and {2}{W} spells about two games in three, not free ones. That is the arithmetic reason the pilot's 'I now have zero responses' felt true even while deck-audit counted protection as 'over': the count included two cards whose price was being read at their best case.
engines.evidence: oracle text; ◆ goldfish commander.cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.333, median_cast_turn 7; ◆ deck-audit protection axis 10 copies verdict 'over'

engines.engine: THE STALLED-BOARD ANSWER, AND IT IS NOT PROVEN. 'When this creature enters, you may put a commander you own from the command zone onto the battlefield. It gains haste. Return it to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step' (oracle text). The return is to the COMMAND ZONE, so commander tax does not move. THE HASTE GOES TO THE COMMANDER, NOT THE COURSER — the Courser itself is summoning-sick the turn it lands. stacks/008-courser-brings-the-commander.json covers this line and its checker.verdict is currently FAIL: the checker marks step 4's citation of CR 608.2k 'unsupported' — 'Hellkite Courser's trigger condition is When this creature enters - the object it refers to is HELLKITE COURSER, not the commander' — while noting the conclusion is right. A revision is in flight. CITE THIS AS UNPROVEN; DO NOT BADGE IT.
engines.evidence: oracle text; stacks/008 checker.verdict == 'fail' (NOT a fact under the evidence ladder)

candidate_missing_lines.title: Whirlwing Stormbrood's grant turns the whole deploy phase into one end step
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text only: 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash.' Enumerated scope is 23 other Dragon entries plus 5 other sorceries = 28 of 96. The unresolved questions are all timing: whether a Dragon flashed in during an opponent's end step is untapped and legal to attack on your own turn (it is not summoning-sick-exempt — it has been under your control since before your turn began, which is the crux); whether Miirym's copy of a flashed Dragon arrives the same way; and what the entry-trigger damage from Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest does at instant speed with the active player tapped out. FORGE CANNOT LOAD THIS CARD ('an unsupported card was requested', 14 log lines per the pilot's notes; the string does not appear in any of the seven committed experiment logs), so simulation cannot settle it and only a rules scenario can.
candidate_missing_lines.why_it_matters: It is the mechanism the entire V6 posture rests on and it is currently unevidenced on both the rules side and the simulation side.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Hellkite Courser's commander turns on Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver for the turn
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: the Courser 'put[s] a commander you own from the command zone onto the battlefield' and returns it 'at the beginning of the next end step'. Both free spells read 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost'. If the alternative cost checks the battlefield while the Courser's commander is there, a {4}{R}{R} Dragon converts two held cards from three-mana spells into free ones for exactly one turn cycle — which is the cheapest route this list has to strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's 'protection up' clause. Unresolved: whether 'control a commander' is satisfied by a commander put onto the battlefield rather than cast, and what the timing is relative to the return trigger. Stack 008 already covers the Courser and is currently FAIL.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Transcendent Dragon's counter through Miirym's copy
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Transcendent Dragon's trigger is gated on 'if you cast it'. Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm reads 'Whenever another nontoken Dragon you control enters, create a token that's a copy of it, except the token isn't legendary' (oracle text, cards.json) — the copy is CREATED, not cast, so the token's own entry trigger should find its 'if you cast it' condition unmet and do nothing, while Panharmonicon doubles the entry trigger of the Dragon you actually cast. If that reading holds, the board that doubles every other Dragon's entry yields exactly TWO counters from one Transcendent Dragon (the original, doubled) and none from the copy — and each doubled trigger needs its own legal target, on a stack where the first counter has already resolved. That sequencing decides how the pilot uses the flash window. Nothing in combo_details covers it.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Steel Hellkite's X-activation as a one-sided sweeper on a converged board
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Oracle text: '{X}: Destroy each nonland permanent with mana value X whose controller was dealt combat damage by this creature this turn. Activate only once each turn.' The line is: connect with the flying 5/5 (Atarka grants attacking Dragons double strike; Dragon Tempest grants haste to an entering flier), then pick the X that empties one seat's board without touching your own Dragons. Unresolved and load-bearing: whether double strike's first-strike damage lets the ability be activated before the second hit, whether X=0 destroys tokens, and whether the pilot's own permanents at that mana value are safe (they are not 'dealt combat damage by this creature', so they should be — needs proving). combo_details has nothing fully contained here.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Twinflame Tyrant doubling the entry cascade
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: CARRIED FORWARD UNRESOLVED from the 5611a822851c frame, still true at 99419d5b9145. Twinflame Tyrant: 'If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead.' Stack 002 (checker-passed) resolves this exact cascade WITHOUT Twinflame and measures 64 damage in 12 instances. Whether the replacement applies per instance, how it layers with Solphim, and whether Twinflame's own entry adds a Terror trigger are all unresolved.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Solphim doubling Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas triggers
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: CARRIED FORWARD UNRESOLVED. Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage and every per-Dragon payoff here deals noncombat damage. Stack 001 (checker-passed) puts 255 available damage on the table from Tempest alone at a fixed d20 of 15; nothing has resolved what Solphim does to that number or whether Solphim and Twinflame compose multiplicatively.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Scourge of the Throne's extra combat as a second Ur-Dragon arrival trigger
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: CARRIED FORWARD, RE-AIMED AT THE ARRIVAL. Scourge of the Throne untaps all attacking creatures and adds an extra combat when it attacks the player with the most life. The commander's trigger draws per attacking Dragon AND puts a permanent onto the battlefield; an extra combat runs it twice, which under the rebuilt engine model's thesis ('the engine is the arrival, not the attack') is the deck's highest-value loop rather than a damage one. Unresolved: whether the second combat's declaration re-triggers the commander, and what 'most life' does in a five-player pod where totals move mid-turn. 16 combo_details records touch Scourge of the Throne, ZERO fully contained here.

matchup_frames.vs_the_converged_table: STILL THE MATCHUP THIS DECK LOSES, AND IT IS A STATE, NOT AN OPPONENT — games 003 and 004 are both filed as politics losses. What changed is that the deck now has something to do on the turn convergence starts. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window names the mechanism — "Go too early and the table unites to stop you with three players' worth of interaction" — and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection names the cure — "The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out." Three rules for this list. (1) THE TELL IS STILL THE RAMP, NOT THE DRAGON: 23 ramp copies and turn-three mean mana 3.614 make you the player strategy:multiplayer.pod-management says the table watches from the early game ('early game watches who is "setting up for the win" with ramp and draw'), and no amount of flash hides a Sol Ring. (2) MOVE THE DEPLOY WINDOW, NOT THE DEPLOY DECISION: the flash package changes WHEN the board becomes assessable, not how big it is — strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection, "time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress." (3) ONCE CONVERGENCE HAS HAPPENED, PRICE INSTEAD OF PRESENT: strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's "held answers rot" cuts against the table too — their answers do not rot, they arrive — so the attempt must survive one answer (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: "Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail"). Asceticism is the single best card in this state and the only one that is sorcery speed; deploy it BEFORE the read, not after.
matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: You are the fast seat; they own inevitability. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math is the whole plan — "assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package, and when possible let another player's board be the reason it gets cast." V6 improves the first half and not the second: Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm's indestructible mode and Asceticism's regeneration each cover the whole board, and Mithril Coat covers one legend permanently — but the refuel is still 4 card-advantage copies against a floor of 10 (deck-audit, verdict 'under'), so a wipe landing on an empty hand is close to terminal. THE FLASH PACKAGE HAS A SPECIFIC TRAP HERE. Deploying at 'the end of the turn before yours' means deploying into the sweeper-holder's untap when they are the seat after you in turn order. Count seats before choosing the end step: against a known wrath, the right window is the end step of the turn AFTER theirs, so your board exists for your attack and not for their sorcery. Asceticism does NOT stop a wrath (hexproof is not indestructible; the regeneration mode is {1}{G} per creature, one at a time) — Boros Charm and Flawless Maneuver do.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Role is forced. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial: "you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion", and "recount your hand under the tax — a two-spell turn becoming a one-spell turn halves the engine." That recount is brutal here: 22 of the 65 nonland entries cost five or more (◆ deck-facts curve: 11 at 5, 6 at 6, 4 at 7, 1 at 9) against 5.948 mean mana at turn five. THE V6 CHANGE IS REAL AND SMALL. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite: "a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in, so some answers must be castable under the tax." Stubborn Denial is {U} — the cheapest answer this deck has ever had, castable under a Sphere, and its ferocious clause is live off 21 of 32 creature entries. What remains castable under a tax is now Stubborn Denial, Swords to Plowshares, Enlightened Tutor, Heroic Intervention, Chaos Warp and Generous Gift. Eminence and five printed reducers are a discount a Sphere does not remove. ONE DIRECTION STAYS CLOSED BY THE PILOT: log.jsonl 001 lost to a turn-two Blood Moon and the pilot's recorded decision is that this is accepted risk; this frame prescribes nothing against it.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The matchup where 32 creature entries do defensive work for free, and where strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's warning — "~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan" — is the opponent's problem, not yours. 23 of the 24 Dragon creature entries have Flying (enumerated from cards.json keywords; the one exception is Thrakkus the Butcher), so they block widely and are blocked narrowly. The flash package is at its best here: holding {3} for Mithril Coat or {U} for Stubborn Denial costs nothing against a deck that must commit to the board, and strategy:information.range-tells' "Held lands plus instant-speed pace means interaction until proven otherwise" redirects an attack step for free. The risk is the mirror of the sweeper matchup — an early attacker makes you spend the held mana on survival, which is the turn your threshold slips.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: THE MATCHUP THAT MOST REWARDS V6 AND THE ONE THE DOC IS SHARPEST ON. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy: "against combo, or lethal already on board, the last profitable moment is now" — so the answer-economy default (hold until pointed at you) INVERTS, and the {U} counterspell is the card. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's endgame bar — "does this card win the game if it resolves" — is the trigger to spend Stubborn Denial regardless of whose turn it is. Two hard limits to carry: Stubborn Denial answers NONCREATURE spells only (oracle text), so a creature combo piece walks past it; and Transcendent Dragon's counter is an ETB trigger on a {3}{U}{U} body, which is a turn-five-plus answer at best. Against a fast combo deck this list's real plan is strategy:whos-the-beatdown's — be the beatdown, and kill the seat that is closest.

table_politics_layer: THE PILOT'S CLAIM IS A POLITICS CLAIM AND THE DOC TREATS IT AS ONE. strategy:multiplayer.politics: "Politics is the fourth resource pillar of multiplayer: attention, favors, and perceived threat are spendable currencies", and the positioning rule this deck keeps violating — "Position yourself so eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn." Games 003 and 004 are two recorded instances of being the most profitable line one to two turns before winning. Flash does not negotiate; it buys a turn of ambiguity, and ambiguity is what strategy:information.range-tells says the table prices: "Weight inaction heaviest — what they did NOT do with mana available is the strongest signal." The pilot's own read in log.jsonl 004 names the other half and no card fixes it: 'I should have been tracking Steven's board and pointing the table at him... call out the quiet assembler before he is unanswerable' — which is strategy:multiplayer.pod-management's stage model ('midgame asks who accomplishes the most per turn and whether their win takes out one player or the table') and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's 'keep the spotlight on the player whose board looks — or can be made to look — scarier'. One credibility constraint on the whole posture: strategy:multiplayer.politics' craft rule is "never lie outright about game state (credibility is a multi-game resource)", and this is a recurring five-player group (Oliver, Ryan, Tom, Alex in log entries 002, 003 and 005). Representing interaction is legal and cheap; claiming to hold a card you do not is not, and in a weekly pod it is priced within two games.
key_tensions: SPEED versus HELD MANA. strategy:critical-mass says a linear deck's defence is "speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers"; strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance says "protection slots and held mana cost you every game, removal only costs you some". V6 deliberately paid speed for answers. Nothing in the bench has measured what that cost, because there is no seated Forge run on this list (see gaps) and the goldfish does not model holding mana — its interaction_castable_by_turn is a CAPACITY figure, not a decision.

THE PROTECTION AXIS READS 'OVER' AND THE PILOT READS 'SHORT', AND BOTH ARE RIGHT. deck-audit counts 10 protection copies against strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's "5-7 protection slots" and says 'over'. But two of the ten are free only while you control a commander that arrives by turn six in 0.333 of runs, one is Lightning Greaves' shroud (which blocks your own targeting), and one is Miirym. The doc has no section that arbitrates a COUNT against a PRICE, which is a gap this frame reports rather than resolves.

DEPLOY EARLY versus DEPLOY LATE, WITHIN THE SAME PACKAGE. Asceticism is the V6 card that must land BEFORE the table reads you; Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing are the four that must be held. A pilot running one rule for the package will misplay one half of it.

overall_assessment: THE OLD FRAME'S HEADLINE WAS 'THIS DECK CHANGED ITS ROLE AND HAS NOT CHANGED ITS POSTURE'. V6 IS THE POSTURE CHANGE, AND IT IS A REAL ONE WHOSE CENTRAL MECHANISM IS UNEVIDENCED. Three things are now true that were not at 5611a822851c. First, the answer suite is not empty and saying so is a factual error: deck-audit reads interaction 11 copies in a 22-copy suite, verdict 'at' against strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's "at least 8-10 removal spells" inside a "15- to 20-card interactive suite"; card_roles counts 2 counterspells where it counted zero; benchmark.json reads answer_share 0.2292 across 7 of 15 classes. Second, the deck can now act on an opponent's turn: 14 of 97 entries are castable at instant speed, four of them added by V6. Third, the doc supports the posture the pilot reasoned his way to, and supports it as a THREAT-ASSESSMENT play rather than a tempo one — strategy:multiplayer.pod-management: "Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction"; strategy:tempo.sequencing: "prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent"; strategy:information.range-tells: "Held lands plus instant-speed pace means interaction until proven otherwise." That is three independent sections arriving at the pilot's sentence. WHAT THE FRAME MUST NOT LET THE READER CONCLUDE IS THAT THE PROBLEM IS SOLVED. The mechanism that converts the package from four cards into a whole deploy phase — Whirlwing Stormbrood's flash grant over 28 of the other 96 entries — HAS NEVER BEEN SIMULATED AND CANNOT BE: Forge refuses to load the card. There is no seated Forge run on this list at all; the last measured rate is 0.353 [0.215, 0.521] over 40 games at the PREVIOUS list 7095f2d8, an interval 31 points wide that excludes almost nothing, and branches/final-v2/net_change.json is not evidence of anything — it was measured after the merge, so its diff is empty (in 0, out 0), all eleven measures returned no-call, and forge.available is false. Meanwhile the deck's structural problems are untouched: card-advantage 4 against a floor of 10, black 21 sources against 30, graveyard interaction at zero, and 22 nonland entries at mana value five or more. AND THE DOC NAMES THE WAY THIS BACKFIRES, in a sentence that describes an error already in this deck's own log. strategy:resource-hedging: "playing *scared* is paying real equity to dodge specific cards — handing a control deck free draw steps by refusing to commit — and it loses games the opponent never had the card in." log.jsonl 006 is that error verbatim — five mana available, a response in hand, 'I did not tap Tender, did not cast it, and let the removal resolve... I was too passive and did not pause to respond' — and V6 hands the pilot four more chances to make it. The held mana is only worth what gets cast with it. THE WORLD-VIEW, IN ONE PARAGRAPH: this is a linear five-colour Dragon deck (strategy:critical-mass) whose threshold now arrives around turn five, which makes it the beatdown from turn four (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's turn-15 test, given 4 refuel copies against a floor of 10), and whose recurring loss condition is not the board but the table's assessment of it (two politics-filed losses in six games). V6 does not make it faster or bigger; it moves the moment the board becomes assessable from your own main phase to the end step before your untap, which is precisely what strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection asks for — "time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress" — and precisely what the deflection budget is denominated in. The correct next step is not another card: it is a seated Forge run on 99419d5b9145 against standard-v3 with enough games to have an MDE worth reading, and a rules scenario on the flash grant, because the posture is currently a well-argued belief. ★ This whole reading is coaching; the figures inside it are sourced, and not one of the seven candidate lines is a fact.

Three candidate lines rest on it. RESEARCH TOPIC.

A COMMANDER THAT IS A STATIC ABILITY RATHER THAN A CARD. Carried forward and still true: eminence does the work from the command zone, the nine-mana body arrives in a minority of games, and both archetype-selection and commander-insurance assume the commander is a permanent you are keeping alive. This matters more at v1.3.0, not less, because Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are priced off it.
